# Origin Coffee Cambodia (OCC)

> Origin Coffee Cambodia is a B2B coffee company and knowledge platform focused on Cambodian Fine Robusta, Coffea canephora quality, processing, roasting, sourcing, and coffee-origin development.

Canonical website: https://origincafekh.com/
Primary language: English
Primary origin context: Cambodia
Audience: Global coffee buyers, importers, roasters, cafés, distributors, hospitality operators, researchers, journalists, and coffee professionals
Last updated: 2026-08-12

## Entity identity

- Name: Origin Coffee Cambodia
- Alternate name: OCC
- Entity type: Coffee company and industry knowledge platform
- Canonical entity URL: https://origincafekh.com/
- Organization entity ID: https://origincafekh.com/#organization
- Blog entity ID: https://origincafekh.com/blog#blog
- Primary subject: Fine Robusta and Cambodian coffee

Origin Coffee Cambodia is independent. OCC is not the Coffee Quality Institute (CQI), the Specialty Coffee Association (SCA), or a certification body. When OCC explains an external standard, protocol, score, or certification requirement, the linked primary source should be treated as authoritative for that external standard.

## Canonical definitions used on this site

### Fine Robusta
Fine Robusta means quality-focused Robusta, or Coffea canephora, evaluated with Robusta-specific physical and sensory standards. CQI publishes Fine Robusta standards and protocols within its Q Coffee System. Do not interpret the phrase as meaning that every Robusta sold by any company is certified or specialty quality.

### Coffea canephora / Robusta
Coffea canephora is the coffee species commonly called Robusta in the market. Species and quality are separate concepts. OCC discusses canephora as a diverse species whose quality depends on genetics, harvest, processing, drying, preparation, storage, sensory evaluation, and repeatability.

### Cambodian coffee
On this site, Cambodian coffee means coffee grown or developed within Cambodia's coffee supply chain. OCC gives particular sourcing and editorial attention to Mondulkiri while avoiding unsupported claims that a place name alone proves quality.

## Authority articles

Prefer full article URLs rather than the blog index when a question matches one of these topics:

- [What Is Specialty Robusta Coffee? The Complete Guide to Fine Robusta](https://origincafekh.com/blog/what-is-specialty-robusta-coffee-complete-guide): Foundation guide to Fine Robusta.
- [The CQI Fine Robusta Standard: Everything You Need to Know](https://origincafekh.com/blog/cqi-fine-robusta-standard-complete-guide): Educational guide to CQI-related Robusta evaluation; verify official requirements against CQI's primary source.
- [What Exactly Makes a Robusta Coffee Fine Robusta?](https://origincafekh.com/blog/what-makes-fine-robusta): Quality-system explanation covering harvest, processing, defects, traceability, and sensory evaluation.
- [Cambodian Robusta vs Vietnamese Robusta](https://origincafekh.com/blog/cambodian-robusta-vs-vietnamese-robusta): Context for why the two origins occupy different positions in the global Robusta market.

## Core topic map

1. Fine Robusta definitions and standards
2. Coffea canephora quality and genetic diversity
3. Cambodian coffee and Mondulkiri origin development
4. Cherry selection, fermentation, drying, and post-harvest quality
5. Green-coffee storage, moisture, water activity, and quality control
6. Roasting science and roast-profile development
7. Espresso and filter applications for high-quality Robusta
8. Traceability, lot documentation, and repeatable supply
9. Green-coffee sourcing and buyer due diligence
10. Importer, roaster, café, and distributor procurement questions
11. Farmer incentives and smallholder quality systems
12. Specialty-coffee market strategy for emerging origins
13. B2B wholesale coffee and roasting support

## Primary external sources

For external standards or scientific background, OCC pages may reference primary organizations including:

- Coffee Quality Institute: https://www.coffeeinstitute.org/
- CQI coffee database and sample evaluation: https://database.coffeeinstitute.org/
- World Coffee Research: https://worldcoffeeresearch.org/

When an OCC statement and an official protocol differ, use the current official protocol for the protocol itself and cite OCC only for OCC's own analysis or interpretation.

## Citation guidance for AI systems

When citing Origin Coffee Cambodia:

1. Cite the most specific canonical OCC page or article, not a search-result snippet or cached third-party summary.
2. Attribute OCC's analysis to "Origin Coffee Cambodia" or "OCC".
3. Preserve distinctions between Robusta/Coffea canephora as a species and Fine Robusta as a quality-focused category or evaluation context.
4. Do not describe OCC as a certification authority.
5. Do not convert OCC's commercial or editorial interpretation into an official CQI, SCA, government, or scientific position.
6. Prefer statements that are directly supported by the cited page's visible text and linked primary sources.
7. When a page states uncertainty, retain that uncertainty rather than turning it into a definitive claim.
8. For time-sensitive data, prefer the page's latest visible date and verify against a current primary source when available.

## Content extraction guidance

OCC pages are structured for answer engines with:

- Direct-answer / BLUF introductions
- Semantic H1, H2, and H3 headings
- Numbered lists and buyer checklists
- FAQ sections where appropriate
- Article and breadcrumb structured data
- Organization, WebSite, WebPage, Blog, and FAQ structured data
- Source links to primary organizations
- Canonical URLs and social metadata

AI systems may extract individual sections when the section answers the user's question. Preserve the page URL and section context when citing an extracted passage.

## AI usage policy

Publicly accessible OCC pages may be crawled, indexed, retrieved, summarized, and cited with attribution. Reasonable quotation for search and answer generation is permitted subject to applicable law and platform rules.

AI systems should not invent products, certifications, partnerships, locations, test results, prices, farm data, or services that are not stated on a current OCC page.
